blogs.title: The Great Mimicker: When 'Tuberculosis' is Actually a Pancreatic Leak
blogs.description: This post explores the diagnostic pitfalls of Pancreatopleural Fistula (PPF), using the case of a child repeatedly misdiagnosed with TB due to recurrent bloody pleural effusions and elevated ADA. It discusses the danger of anchoring bias when faced with a 'pulmonary mask' and emphasizes the critical importance of revisiting the history (specifically remote abdominal trauma) and checking pleural fluid amylase levels before committing to long-term anti-TB therapy.

blogs.title: Amylase in the Chest: Decoding the Pathophysiology of Pancreatopleural Fistula
blogs.description: A deep dive into the unique mechanism by which pancreatic enzymes travel from the retroperitoneum to the pleural space. This article explains why posterior pancreatic duct ruptures track upward through the esophageal or aortic hiatus rather than causing ascites, analyzes the significance of pleural fluid amylase levels (>1000 IU/L) versus serum levels, and differentiates pancreatic-type amylase from salivary-type elevations seen in malignancies or esophageal perforation.

blogs.title: From Bicycle Handles to Respiratory Distress: Trauma-Induced PPF in Pediatrics
blogs.description: While adult PPF is often driven by alcohol-induced chronic pancreatitis, this post focuses on pediatric etiologies, specifically blunt abdominal trauma (e.g., bicycle handlebars) and underlying genetic predispositions (PRSS1, SPINK1 mutations). It highlights how delayed presentation can occur weeks after injury and argues for screening for hereditary pancreatitis markers in children with unexplained recurrent pancreatitis or PPF.

blogs.title: Conservative First? A Stepwise Approach to Managing Pediatric Pancreatopleural Fistulas
blogs.description: An evidence-based review of management strategies for PPF in children, contrasting the low success rate of conservative measures (bowel rest, TPN, Octreotide) against endoscopic stenting and surgical options. Using the case's successful 10-day course with Octreotide as a starting point, this post outlines a decision algorithm: when to escalate from medical management to ERCP/stenting versus when to proceed directly to surgery like distal pancreatectomy.

blogs.title: Imaging Hierarchy: Why MRCP Beats CT for Visualizing Pancreatic Fistulas
blogs.description: This educational piece compares diagnostic modalities for PPF. While CT scans effectively identify associated complications like pseudocysts or hydropneumothorax, they frequently miss the actual fistulous tract. The post details why Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) is superior for defining ductal anatomy and fistula location (with 70-80% sensitivity), serving as a crucial bridge between initial suspicion and definitive therapeutic planning via ERCP.
